{{Short description|Algebraic plane curve}}
{{distinguish|Butterfly curve (transcendental)}}
{{no footnotes|date=August 2026}}

[[File:Butterfly curve.png|thumb|The butterfly curve <math>x^6 + y^6 = x^2</math>]]
[[File:Butterlink.png|thumb|The butterfly curve singularity [[link (knot theory)|link]]]]

In [[mathematics]], the '''algebraic butterfly curve''' is a [[algebraic curve|plane algebraic curve]] of [[Degree of an algebraic variety|degree]] six given by the equation
:<math> x^6 + y^6 = x^2.</math>  

The butterfly curve has a single [[mathematical singularity|singularity]] with [[delta invariant]] three, which means it is a curve of [[geometric genus|genus]] seven. The only plane curves of genus seven are singular, since seven is not a [[triangular number]], and the minimum degree for such a curve is six.

The butterfly curve has branching number and multiplicity two, and hence the singularity [[link (knot theory)|link]] has two components.

The area of the algebraic butterfly curve is given by
:<math>4 \int_0^1 (x^2 - x^6)^{\frac{1}{6}} dx = \frac{ \Gamma\big(\frac{1}{6}\big) \cdot \Gamma\big(\frac{1}{3}\big)}{3 \sqrt{\pi}} \approx 2.804,</math>
where <math>\Gamma</math> is the [[gamma function]], and the [[arc length]] of the curve is <math>s \approx 9.017</math>.
